texts: good. parses as a two-member group with its count, a group-level departure, and a per-member rule, so a Keeper named later still gets her own leaving.

mixed: the structure is clean — a counted pair marrying in one event, with "outside" kept as a surface preposition rather than folded into an in-ness claim — but it reads "outside Aelmere" as the place the wedding happened. If you meant they married people from outside the village, which is what the surrounding departure rules suggest, that content is lost; rewrite as "The two Keepers married people from outside Aelmere."

mixed: the rule fires and carries the whole policy, but the station lands in two wrong slots — filed as where the Keeper came from rather than as what she leaves, and as the recipient of a transfer rather than as the destination — and the assignment is keyed to the Keeper-and-station pair rather than to the occasion, so two separate departures from one station collapse into a single assignment. Rewrite as "Whenever a Keeper leaves a station, the Council assigns an apprentice to that station." — the explicit "whenever" forces one assignment per departure and the link back to the departure that triggered it. The two slot choices are ours to fix and need nothing from you.

mixed: the parse is a faithful record of one assignment, but it reads as a specific past event — some particular apprentice really did complete thirty solo nights and really was assigned — so the eligibility criterion you are stating is lost, and nothing in the result says what qualifies an apprentice. Rewrite as "When an apprentice has completed thirty solo nights, the Council may assign that apprentice." — the conditional turns the qualification into a rule that fires for any apprentice who meets it, instead of asserting one who did.
